title: My AI agent vs Claude: Trading Battle
author: Mr_Hodlerr
selftext:
**The setup**

On Oct. 9 I opened a $50,000 paper portfolio and let my AI agent trade it in BTC and ETH. Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 each got the same $50,000 from the same close.

\- BTC and ETH only. Spot, no leverage, no shorts

\- One decision a day at the daily close, filled at the Coinbase close

\- Same costs for everyone: 0.06% fee plus 0.01% slippage per trade

\- Optional stop loss for the next day

\- Claude sees a year of daily candles up to that close, its portfolio, what holding would be worth and its last 10 notes. 

\- Benchmark: half BTC, half ETH bought on day one and never touched

  
**After 19 days (Oct. 9 to Oct. 27 close)**

\- My AI: $49,174 (-1.65%), worst drop 2.3%, net trading volume $46,625

\- Claude Fable 5.1: $48,309 (-3.38%), worst drop 4.5%, net trading volume $141,591

\- Claude Opus 5.5: $47,764 (-4.47%), worst drop 5.9%, net trading volume $147,947

\- Buy and hold: $48,047 (-3.91%), worst drop 6.4%, net trading volume $50,000



**A few things that stood out**

\- **The worst days.** On the market's three worst days (Oct. 12, 14 and 22), holding lost $1,490, $1,241 and $1,686. My AI lost $532, $414 and $509, about one third each time.

\- **Claude read ETH right.** Fable flagged ETH as the weaker coin on day one (ETH just broke lower) and held none of it on 14 of 19 days. It was right: over the battle ETH is down 5.6% and BTC 2.1%.

\- **Fable's best move was sitting still.** It went fully to cash on Oct. 24. Holding dipped another 1.2% over the next two days while Fable stayed at $48,309 and that's why it's ahead of holding today.

\- **Same company, different personalities.** Same prompt, same prices, and the two Claude models still trade very differently. Fable has been fully in cash on 4 days. Opus has never been less than 35% invested and has always held some ETH.



**What it costs to run**

Claude's API bill for the 19 decisions was $5.76 (Fable) and $2.15 (Opus). It's the same whether the account holds $100 or $1M, and it only pays for the thinking. Someone still has to place the orders.

My AI runs on Botsfolio, which on real money charges a share of what's traded instead, so the cost grows with the account: $0.23 on $100, $2.33 on $1,000, $80 on this $50k. Even after paying that $80, it's about $790 ahead of the better Claude.



Full trading battle report: [https://botsfolio.com/blog/can-claude-trade-crypto](https://botsfolio.com/blog/can-claude-trade-crypto)  
  
Watch the battle: [https://botsfolio.com/blog/can-claude-trade-crypto#battle](https://botsfolio.com/blog/can-claude-trade-crypto#battle)

Looking at the moves, what do you think each AI is getting right or wrong?

replies.author: Mr_Hodlerr
replies.body:
No did way more than system prompts.  
  
Binance has those fees if you have the volume and BNB,  Coinbase on volume. But if we take Binance's standard fee 0.1% then it won't make that much of a difference.  
I think I did a 0.05%-0.9% spread and saw at worst yearly return was shaved by 17% for 0.9% (AI is already optimized for maker/taker fees by using market and limit orders)

comments.author: fleatedplutmting
comments.body:
This is exactly the kind of AI trading experiment we like seeing!

What's interesting isn't just that your bot is outperforming the Claude models, but that it's managed a significantly smaller drawdown too. 2.3% compared to 6.4% for buy and hold is a pretty decent difference.

We're building AI trading bot tools at EXOS, so experiments like this are right up our alley.

Curious though, are all the models operating under the same risk management and position sizing rules, or does each AI make those decisions independently?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: you added the benchmark this time, which was my gripe last round, so credit for that. with it in, the costs are not the story: Fable's $141k of volume at 0.07% a trade is about $100, a rounding error on a $50k book. the drops are the story, 4.5% and 5.9% against your agent's 2.3% from the same two coins over the same 19 days. is that gap sizing, or the next-day stop doing the work?
